request: How is the Highway Trust Fund financed, and when is it projected to run short of money?

reply.reply:
**The Highway Trust Fund is financed mainly by gasoline and diesel taxes plus other transportation excise taxes; CBO projects its mass transit account will approach zero in FY2027 and highway account in FY2028.**

- Under current trends, CBO projects the mass transit account will approach zero in FY2027 and the highway account in FY2028; the Fund cannot have a negative balance. (R48948, PDF p. 7)
- The Fund is financed primarily by federal per-gallon gasoline and diesel taxes, with portions allocated to highway and mass transit accounts. (R48472, PDF p. 6)
- Fuel taxes account for roughly 85% of annual highway-account revenue; other transportation-related excise taxes also contribute. (R48472, PDF p. 6)
reply.reasoning: Recent CRS evidence identifies both the principal revenue sources and the account-level CBO balance projections, which provide a direct answer to how the Fund is financed and when it is projected to run short.
